near_miss.lead: ON myrkt (af nótt) ~ Serbian мркла ноћ / ноћи мрака: *merkʷ-/mergʷ- 'dark' + *nokʷt- 'night'
near_miss.why_not: ON myrkr and Slavic mrak/mrkъ are plausibly cognate and night is cognate, but 'dark night' is semantically trivial and recurs independently everywhere; ON 'gerði myrkt af nótt' is a saga prose idiom (also Grettis s., Jómsvíkinga s.); Eddic myrkr pairs rather with forest (myrkvan við, Myrkviðr) and OE myrce never occurs with niht in Grein/Beowulf; Serbian мркла ноћ (10x in Vuk) is a late stock epithet. No congruent context beyond 'it was night'.

near_miss.lead: kin-term pairs (sister + daughter; father + mother; mother's sister) built from inherited kinship nouns
near_miss.why_not: Inherited kinship vocabulary co-occurs by necessity in genealogies; the Egils saga lines are prose genealogy ('X dóttir, systir Y'), with no shared figure, ordering or syntax beyond coordination. 'faðir ok móðir' ~ pitṛ-mātṛ is a universal pairing (and the Skt order is mātṛ-pitṛ / pitṛ mātṛṣu in different construction). Generic.

near_miss.lead: ON vatni ausa ('sprinkle with water', naming rite) ~ Gk ἀφυσσάμεθ' ὕδωρ 'we drew water' (*h2ews- + *wodr-)
near_miss.why_not: Contexts incongruent (child-naming lustration vs. drawing water on landfall); ON uses instrumental vatni 'sprinkle with water', Greek accusative 'draw water'; derivation of ἀφύσσω from *h2ews- is doubtful (no secure etymology). The real *h2ews- + water collocation would be Lat. aquam haurire ~ ON ausa vatn 'bail', but that is not in these bundles and is everyday language. Il. 11.462 is a mapping artefact (shout).

near_miss.lead: ON stóð upp ... við sól ~ Ved. ā́ sū́ryo ... tiṣṭhat: *steh2- + *sóh2wl̥
near_miss.why_not: In ON the man rises at sunrise (sól in a temporal PP), in RV the sun mounts/stands (sun is subject); different syntax and referent. Sun-rise with 'stand' is a natural metaphor; no shared wording.

near_miss.lead: ON fell snjór (mikill) ~ Umbr. ninctu (imprecation verb 'snow upon'), also νυκτός / mahat
near_miss.why_not: ON falla is not cognate with Umbr. holtu; ON is a narrative weather report, Umbrian a curse list of afflictions on the enemy. Only *sneygwh- shared, in incongruent contexts.

near_miss.lead: body-part list 'eyes and nose' (augu ok nasar ~ oculis naribus ~ око нос)
near_miss.why_not: Lists of face parts are generic; Egill's vomit into Ármóðr's face, Lucretius' senses and a bylina description share no figure or syntax.

near_miss.lead: season terms vár / sumar ~ vasanta / (samā) in season sequences
near_miss.why_not: ON uses two seasons as narrative time adverbials ('um várit ... um sumarit'); AV gives a ritual list of six seasons. Cognate season names are lexical inheritance, not phraseology; no shared figure.

near_miss.lead: ON byr gaf ('a fair wind was given')
near_miss.why_not: Partner (Theban horned snakes) shares only *bher-/*h1es- by root; nothing congruent. Empty bundle.

near_miss.lead: ON lǫgðusk niðr ... sváfu um nóttina ~ Ru. легъ спать на темную ночь: *legh- + *swep- + *nokwt-
near_miss.why_not: All three cognates are basic vocabulary (lie down, sleep, night) that must co-occur whenever someone goes to bed; ON is plain prose (in straw in a barn), the bylina line is a stock transition formula; Russian adds the epithet темная, absent in ON. Not distinguishable from chance/generic language.

near_miss.lead: hǫfuð ... fót (head ... foot) ~ capite aut pedibus
near_miss.why_not: ON: bring the king your head and clasp his foot (submission gesture); Lucretius: anatomical locus of mind. Head-foot co-occurrence is generic; no shared figure.

near_miss.lead: ON egg øxinni 'edge of the axe' ~ Gk ὀξέσι ... ἀξίνῃσι 'sharp axes': *h2eḱ- + *h2egwsih2
near_miss.why_not: Both roots are cognate, but ON has a noun (edge, looked at) and Greek an adjective (sharp axes, fought with): different construction and context; 'sharp axe' is semantically automatic and Greek ὀξύς is the default sharpness adjective. No ON *hvass/egg + øx formula found that would make it a fixed collocation.

error.correct_reading: egg f. 'edge (of a blade)' < *h2eḱ-; the h₂ōwyóm 'egg' alternative is a homograph error
error.evidence: 'sá í egg øxinni' = looked at the edge of the axe

error.correct_reading: ἀΰω 'shout' (aor. ἤϋσε), of onomatopoeic origin (cf. ἀϋτή); not *h2ews-
error.evidence: context: τρὶς μὲν ἔπειτ' ἤϋσεν ... τρὶς δ' ἄϊεν ἰάχοντος (shouting/hearing)

error.correct_reading: personal name Bjǫrn (subject of sagði), should be (name)
personal name Bera (gen.), Egill's mother, should be (name); not the verb bera
